## Complete current assessment

Reviewed the complete two-file M1 implementation and tests at9b36473e, including all corrections to the original a35656ec..5aafb7aa slice, against unchanged Design r5, Delivery r2 and TNI-DES-02–05/TG-01. This judgment is independent of author claims and earlier negative reviews. The helper remains unconnected to public init, so trust/archive eligibility and user-facing installation proof stay in M2. Existing recorded workflow-to-route/public behavior remains unaffected.

No remaining material defect was found within this private synchronous helper boundary. The correction combines original filesystem authority checks, pinned-parent basename mutations, atomic no-clobber public publication, both-endpoint detachment, and retained original/recovery paths. These mechanisms address the actual failure causes rather than relying only on before/after snapshots. Fresh private names prevent normal competing writes from sharing backup destinations; this is not a claim of OS authentication, isolation against code controlling the same process, or a new security service.

## Original reporter disposition

Original reporter resolves m1-review-f2 against complete current M1 files at9b36473e. Captured root/containing-parent dev/ino authority rejects substituted project namespaces; verified immediate-parent cwd pinning keeps public basename mutations off replaced ancestors. Directory creation no longer reopens/chmods a mutable public path and restores caller umask. Both detachment endpoints are now basenames under the same pinned parent, eliminating absolute-stage backup/rollback destinations. Fresh unadvertised256-bit sibling names define private retained destinations outside selected roots, with explicit collision rejection and retainedPaths returned on success/failure. Existing deterministic tests demonstrate public child-link and restoration ancestor preservation, directory/symlink root replacement rejection, and independent destination-byte preservation during final backup/rollback rename. All33 focused cases independently pass, including f1 protections. This resolves the observed private-helper authority failures; M2 public wiring, backup diagnostics and integrated recovery remain mandatory downstream allocation.

## Checklist coverage

| Item | Assessment | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spec alignment | pass for M1 | Implements allocated original-basis, safe selected-root, no-clobber publication and conflict-aware recovery support under TNI-DES-02–05. |
| Test coverage | pass for M1 |33 focused cases cover initial validation, ten failure checkpoints, installed verification, missing state, symlinks, scope, concurrent writes and meaningful namespace regressions. |
| Edge cases | pass for M1 | Explicit normal/retry/rollback and both OpenCode-style roots; ancestor/root and final-syscall substitutions preserve protected outside data. |
| Error handling | pass for M1 | Caught failures restore original pair when safe; conflicting changes retain storage and report recovery-required, with actual retainedPaths available. |
| Architecture boundaries | pass | Private helper only; archive trust and recorded eligibility remain caller responsibility, no public record/schema or service change. |
| Compatibility | pass within slice | No public dispatch connected; original lock/hash contracts retained. M2 still must prove actual upgrade and unchanged other installer paths. |
| Security/privacy | pass within scope | Closed state fields, contained paths, original identity checks, pinned parents and no public path chmod; unrelated state/content preservation has targeted regression evidence. |
| Derived artifact currency | pass within slice | Existing dist library/test scope only; no new source/generated skill or installed candidate claim. |
| Unrelated changes | pass | Two allocated implementation/test files plus author/reviewer evidence; no historical model/ADR rewrite or M2 implementation. |
| Validation evidence | pass for M1 | Independently executed33 focused tests; current exact author evidence supplies433 full Node and7 publication passes. |

The test changes retain meaningful prior protection and add regressions that failed before their respective corrections. Test fixtures assert intended persistent bytes/modes and unchanged neighbors; lower-level proof is explicitly limited and cannot replace public CLI installation/fault-recovery evidence.

## Validation and limits

Independently ran node --test packages/rigorloop/test/managed-authoring-replacement.test.js:33 passed. Inspected current m1-both-endpoints-correction evidence for npm test --prefix packages/rigorloop:433 passed and python scripts/test-npm-package-publication.py:7 passed; those full suites were not rerun by reviewer. No external testing or customer installations were performed, and no new counterexample development was part of this final rereview. Record-store validation and git diff --check follow save.

M2 must surface backupPath/retainedPaths and operator recovery guidance, preserve external operator backup requirements, connect eligibility/guards to the helper, and execute all plan-defined public and integrated proof. Retaining private inode storage is not a substitute for the external backup contract. The helper uses synchronous main-thread process cwd/umask sections; that existing CLI execution constraint remains material to integration. This approval is neither M2 approval nor fresh whole-change Code Review or final Verify. Earlier negative judgments and immutable finding origins are preserved.

## Independence

Concrete independent nonauthor task /root/independent_design_review reviews primary-agent implementation of M1. Reviewer authored neither implementation nor tests, inspected complete new files and exact commit diff, and ran a disposable deterministic interleaving reproduction without editing reviewed files. Prior independent Design/Delivery assessments do not substitute for this implementation judgment.
